title.en: [M1] DSA + reading + lab: Distributed systems fundamentals
title.pt-BR: [M1] DSA + leitura + laboratório: Fundamentos de sistemas distribuídos

description.en:
Module 1: Distributed systems fundamentals.
Start with 10 min of flashcard review in Anki (due cards only).

DSA (30 min):
- Two Sum (hash map): https://leetcode.com/problems/two-sum/
- Two Sum II (two pointers on a sorted array): https://leetcode.com/problems/two-sum-ii-input-array-is-sorted/
Timebox 30 min, no AI. Stuck after 20 min: read only the approach in the editorial, then code it yourself and mark the problem "redo".

Reading (2 h):
- Course text: Failures, timeouts and time (written for this course): read this first. It explains the day's concepts and says which sections of the references below to read next. https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/lessons/01-distributed-systems-fundamentals/day-1.md
- Jacob Gabrielson, AWS Builders' Library, "Challenges with distributed systems" (free): the eight failure modes of a request/reply and the UNKNOWN outcome. Write down the 3 possible outcomes of a timeout. https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/challenges-with-distributed-systems/
- Marc Brooker, AWS Builders' Library, "Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter" (free): how Amazon picks timeout values, and why retries need idempotency, backoff and jitter. Note how you'll pick the partner bank timeout. https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/timeouts-retries-and-backoff-with-jitter/
- Google, Site Reliability Engineering, "Chapter 4 - Service Level Objectives" (free): SLI, SLO and SLA definitions and why 100% is the wrong target (the Chubby story). https://sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives/
- John Graham-Cumming, Cloudflare blog, "How and why the leap second affected Cloudflare DNS" (free): a real outage caused by a clock going backward. Note why durations must use a monotonic clock. https://blog.cloudflare.com/how-and-why-the-leap-second-affected-cloudflare-dns/
- Spencer Kimball and Irfan Sharif, Cockroach Labs blog, "Living without atomic clocks" (free): clock skew between servers and the causal reverse anomaly. Write down why you can't order events by wall clock. https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/living-without-atomic-clocks/
- Apache Cassandra documentation, "Dynamo" (free): read the Failure Detection section: how a real database decides a peer is down. https://cassandra.apache.org/doc/latest/cassandra/architecture/dynamo.html
- Alex Entin, Cockroach Labs blog, "Clock Management in CockroachDB: Good Timekeeping is Key" (free): slewing, leap second smearing, VM pauses and the maximum clock offset in production. https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/clock-management-cockroachdb/
- chrony documentation, "chronyc" (free): read the makestep and tracking entries: slewing vs. stepping, and clock drift in ppm. https://chrony-project.org/doc/3.4/chronyc.html
- PostgreSQL documentation, "Sequence Manipulation Functions" (free): read the caution box: why sequence values have gaps and are not commit order. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-sequence.html
- Laurenz Albe, Cybertec, "Gaps in sequences in PostgreSQL" (free): where sequence gaps come from, and how a single-row counter gives a gapless, ordered sequence. Note how your ledger orders one account's entries. https://www.cybertec-postgresql.com/en/gaps-in-sequences-postgresql/
- Jeff Hodges, "Notes on Distributed Systems for Young Bloods" (free): short practical essay; read it if time is left. https://www.somethingsimilar.com/2013/01/14/notes-on-distributed-systems-for-young-bloods/

Lab (1 h):
Create the public repo (services/, docs/, chaos/) with the NestJS skeleton and Docker Compose with a Postgres primary + async replica (streaming replication).
In labs, use AI only to clarify concepts, never to write TCM code.

Flashcards guide: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/FLASHCARDS.md
DSA track: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/DSA.md
Module page: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/modules/01-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md
description.pt-BR:
Módulo 1: Fundamentos de sistemas distribuídos.
Comece com 10 min de revisão de flashcards no Anki (só os pendentes).

DSA (30 min):
- Two Sum (hash map): https://leetcode.com/problems/two-sum/
- Two Sum II (two pointers em array ordenado): https://leetcode.com/problems/two-sum-ii-input-array-is-sorted/
Limite de 30 min, sem IA. Travou depois de 20 min: leia só a abordagem no editorial, depois codifique você mesmo e marque o problema como "refazer".

Leitura (2 h):
- Texto do curso: Falhas, timeouts e tempo (escrito para este curso): leia este primeiro. Ele explica os conceitos do dia e indica quais seções das referências abaixo ler em seguida. https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/lessons/01-distributed-systems-fundamentals/day-1.pt-BR.md
- Jacob Gabrielson, AWS Builders' Library, "Challenges with distributed systems" (gratuito): os oito modos de falha de uma requisição/resposta e o desfecho UNKNOWN. Anote os 3 desfechos possíveis de um timeout. https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/challenges-with-distributed-systems/
- Marc Brooker, AWS Builders' Library, "Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter" (gratuito): como a Amazon escolhe valores de timeout, e por que retries precisam de idempotência, backoff e jitter. Anote como você vai escolher o timeout do banco parceiro. https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/timeouts-retries-and-backoff-with-jitter/
- Google, Site Reliability Engineering, "Chapter 4 - Service Level Objectives" (gratuito): definições de SLI, SLO e SLA e por que 100% é a meta errada (a história do Chubby). https://sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives/
- John Graham-Cumming, blog da Cloudflare, "How and why the leap second affected Cloudflare DNS" (gratuito): uma queda real causada por um relógio que andou para trás. Anote por que durações precisam usar um relógio monotônico. https://blog.cloudflare.com/how-and-why-the-leap-second-affected-cloudflare-dns/
- Spencer Kimball e Irfan Sharif, blog da Cockroach Labs, "Living without atomic clocks" (gratuito): diferença entre relógios de servidores e a anomalia causal reverse. Anote por que você não pode ordenar eventos pelo relógio de parede. https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/living-without-atomic-clocks/
- Documentação do Apache Cassandra, "Dynamo" (gratuito): leia a seção Failure Detection: como um banco de dados real decide que um par caiu. https://cassandra.apache.org/doc/latest/cassandra/architecture/dynamo.html
- Alex Entin, blog da Cockroach Labs, "Clock Management in CockroachDB: Good Timekeeping is Key" (gratuito): slewing, smearing de leap seconds, pausas de VM e o offset máximo de relógio em produção. https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/clock-management-cockroachdb/
- Documentação do chrony, "chronyc" (gratuito): leia as entradas makestep e tracking: slewing vs. stepping, e deriva do relógio em ppm. https://chrony-project.org/doc/3.4/chronyc.html
- Documentação do PostgreSQL, "Sequence Manipulation Functions" (gratuito): leia o quadro de cuidado: por que valores de sequence têm buracos e não são a ordem de commit. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-sequence.html
- Laurenz Albe, Cybertec, "Gaps in sequences in PostgreSQL" (gratuito): de onde vêm os buracos em sequences, e como um contador em uma única linha dá uma sequência ordenada e sem buracos. Anote como seu ledger ordena os lançamentos de uma conta. https://www.cybertec-postgresql.com/en/gaps-in-sequences-postgresql/
- Jeff Hodges, "Notes on Distributed Systems for Young Bloods" (gratuito): ensaio prático e curto; leia se sobrar tempo. https://www.somethingsimilar.com/2013/01/14/notes-on-distributed-systems-for-young-bloods/

Laboratório (1 h):
Crie o repositório público (services/, docs/, chaos/) com o esqueleto NestJS e o Docker Compose com Postgres primário + réplica assíncrona (streaming replication).
Nos laboratórios, IA só para tirar dúvida de conceito, nunca para escrever código do TCM.

Guia de flashcards: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/FLASHCARDS.pt-BR.md
Trilha de DSA: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/DSA.pt-BR.md
Página do módulo: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/modules/01-distributed-systems-fundamentals.pt-BR.md

description.en:
Module 1: Distributed systems fundamentals.

DSA (30 min):
- 3Sum (sort + two pointers, generalizes to k-sum): https://leetcode.com/problems/3sum/
Timebox 30 min, no AI. Stuck after 20 min: read only the approach in the editorial, then code it yourself and mark the problem "redo".

Reading (2 h):
- Course text: Replication and replication lag (written for this course): read this first. It explains the day's concepts and says which sections of the references below to read next. https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/lessons/01-distributed-systems-fundamentals/day-2.md
- PostgreSQL documentation, "High Availability, Load Balancing, and Replication" (free): leader/follower, synchronous vs. asynchronous replication, failover and the writes you lose on failover. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/high-availability.html
- PostgreSQL documentation, "Log-Shipping Standby Servers" (free): streaming replication (including Monitoring) and Synchronous Replication: what each synchronous_commit level guarantees and how to measure lag with LSNs. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
- MongoDB manual, "Read Isolation, Consistency, and Recency" (free): read your writes and monotonic reads defined, and why secondary reads are stale but never out of order. Write one violation of each in a wallet app. https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/read-isolation-consistency-recency/
- MongoDB manual, "Causal Consistency and Read and Write Concerns" (free): the network partition scenarios: why w:1 writes can be rolled back and majority writes cannot. https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/causal-consistency-read-write-concerns/
- Microsoft, Azure Cosmos DB documentation, "Consistency levels in Azure Cosmos DB" (free): session consistency and session tokens, consistent prefix, and the RPO table. Note how a session token gives read-your-writes. https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cosmos-db/consistency-levels
- Apache Cassandra documentation, "Dynamo" (free): leaderless replication, tunable consistency levels and quorums (W + R > RF), read repair, hinted handoff and last write wins. https://cassandra.apache.org/doc/latest/cassandra/architecture/dynamo.html

Lab (1 h):
Stale-read experiment (short version): a script writes to the primary and reads from the replica in a loop, measuring lag; put Toxiproxy between them to make lag visible.
In labs, use AI only to clarify concepts, never to write TCM code.

DSA track: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/DSA.md
Module page: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/modules/01-distributed-systems-fundamentals.md
description.pt-BR:
Módulo 1: Fundamentos de sistemas distribuídos.

DSA (30 min):
- 3Sum (ordenação + two pointers, generaliza para k-sum): https://leetcode.com/problems/3sum/
Limite de 30 min, sem IA. Travou depois de 20 min: leia só a abordagem no editorial, depois codifique você mesmo e marque o problema como "refazer".

Leitura (2 h):
- Texto do curso: Replicação e replication lag (escrito para este curso): leia este primeiro. Ele explica os conceitos do dia e indica quais seções das referências abaixo ler em seguida. https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/lessons/01-distributed-systems-fundamentals/day-2.pt-BR.md
- Documentação do PostgreSQL, "High Availability, Load Balancing, and Replication" (gratuito): líder/seguidor, replicação síncrona vs. assíncrona, failover e as escritas que você perde no failover. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/high-availability.html
- Documentação do PostgreSQL, "Log-Shipping Standby Servers" (gratuito): streaming replication (incluindo Monitoring) e Synchronous Replication: o que cada nível de synchronous_commit garante e como medir o lag com LSNs. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html
- Manual do MongoDB, "Read Isolation, Consistency, and Recency" (gratuito): read your writes e monotonic reads definidos, e por que leituras em secundários ficam desatualizadas mas nunca fora de ordem. Anote uma violação de cada em um app de carteira. https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/read-isolation-consistency-recency/
- Manual do MongoDB, "Causal Consistency and Read and Write Concerns" (gratuito): os cenários de partição de rede: por que escritas w:1 podem sofrer rollback e escritas majority não. https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/causal-consistency-read-write-concerns/
- Microsoft, documentação do Azure Cosmos DB, "Consistency levels in Azure Cosmos DB" (gratuito): consistência session e session tokens, consistent prefix e a tabela de RPO. Anote como um session token dá read your writes. https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cosmos-db/consistency-levels
- Documentação do Apache Cassandra, "Dynamo" (gratuito): replicação sem líder, consistency levels ajustáveis e quorums (W + R > RF), read repair, hinted handoff e last write wins. https://cassandra.apache.org/doc/latest/cassandra/architecture/dynamo.html

Laboratório (1 h):
Experimento de leitura velha: script que escreve no primário e lê na réplica em loop, medindo o lag. Coloque o Toxiproxy entre as duas para tornar o lag visível. Anote os números.
Nos laboratórios, IA só para tirar dúvida de conceito, nunca para escrever código do TCM.

Trilha de DSA: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/DSA.pt-BR.md
Página do módulo: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/modules/01-distributed-systems-fundamentals.pt-BR.md

Ele explica os conceitos do dia e indica quais seções das referências abaixo ler em seguida.
- [Documentação do PostgreSQL, "High Availability, Load Balancing, and Replication"](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/high-availability.html) *(gratuito)*: líder/seguidor, replicação síncrona vs. assíncrona, failover e as escritas que você perde no failover.
- [Documentação do PostgreSQL, "Log-Shipping Standby Servers"](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html) *(gratuito)*: streaming replication (incluindo Monitoring) e Synchronous Replication: o que cada nível de `synchronous_commit` garante e como medir o lag com LSNs.
- [Manual do MongoDB, "Read Isolation, Consistency, and Recency"](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/read-isolation-consistency-recency/) *(gratuito)*: read your writes e monotonic reads definidos, e por que leituras em secundários ficam desatualizadas mas nunca fora de ordem. Anote uma violação de cada em um app de carteira.
- [Manual do MongoDB, "Causal Consistency and Read and Write Concerns"](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/causal-consistency-read-write-concerns/) *(gratuito)*: os cenários de partição de rede: por que escritas w:1 podem sofrer rollback e escritas majority não.
- [Microsoft, documentação do Azure Cosmos DB, "Consistency levels in Azure Cosmos DB"](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cosmos-db/consistency-levels) *(gratuito)*: consistência session e session tokens, consistent prefix e a tabela de RPO. Anote como um session token dá read your writes.
- [Documentação do Apache Cassandra, "Dynamo"](https://cassandra.apache.org/doc/latest/cassandra/architecture/dynamo.html) *(gratuito)*: replicação sem líder, consistency levels ajustáveis e quorums (W + R > RF), read repair, hinted handoff e last write wins.

#### Laboratório (1 h)
Experimento de leitura velha: script que escreve no primário e lê na réplica em loop, medindo o lag. Coloque o Toxiproxy entre as duas para tornar o lag visível. Anote os números.
Nos laboratórios, IA só para tirar dúvida de conceito, nunca para escrever código do TCM.

description.en:
Module 3: Transactions, concurrency and Postgres.
Start with 10 min of flashcard review in Anki (due cards only).

DSA (30 min):
- Subarray Sum Equals K (prefix sum + hash map): https://leetcode.com/problems/subarray-sum-equals-k/
Timebox 30 min, no AI. Stuck after 20 min: read only the approach in the editorial, then code it yourself and mark the problem "redo".

Reading (2 h):
- Course text: Isolation levels and the anomalies they allow (written for this course): read this first. It explains the day's concepts and says which sections of the references below to read next. https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/lessons/03-transactions-concurrency-postgres/day-1.md
- Martin Kleppmann, "Hermitage: testing transaction isolation levels" (free): the table of anomalies per database; focus on the PostgreSQL rows, then open postgres.md for the session-by-session commands. https://github.com/ept/hermitage
- PostgreSQL wiki, "SSI" (free): practical write-skew scripts you can paste into psql: Overview, Black and White, Intersecting Data, Overdraft Protection and Deposit Report, at REPEATABLE READ vs. SERIALIZABLE. https://wiki.postgresql.org/wiki/SSI
- Cockroach Labs blog, "What write skew looks like" (free): lost update vs. write skew, and phantoms. Then build your own write-skew example with balances. https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/what-write-skew-looks-like/
- PostgreSQL documentation, "Transaction Isolation" (free): today only the introduction, the phenomena definitions and Table 13.1: what each level allows in Postgres and what ACID really promises for money. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html

Lab (1 h):
Two psql sessions: reproduce a lost update under READ COMMITTED. Write down the exact command sequence.
In labs, use AI only to clarify concepts, never to write TCM code.

description.en:
Module 4: Sagas, Outbox and distributed transactions.
Start with 10 min of flashcard review in Anki (due cards only).

DSA (30 min):
- Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days (binary search on the answer (capacity, days, weights)): https://leetcode.com/problems/capacity-to-ship-packages-within-d-days/
Timebox 30 min, no AI. Stuck after 20 min: read only the approach in the editorial, then code it yourself and mark the problem "redo".

Reading (2 h):
- Course text: Two-phase commit and why sagas exist (written for this course): read this first. It explains the day's concepts and says which sections of the references below to read next. https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/lessons/04-sagas-outbox/day-1.md
- Chris Richardson, microservices.io, "Pattern: Saga" (free): orchestrated vs. choreographed sagas and compensating transactions. https://microservices.io/patterns/data/saga.html
- PostgreSQL documentation, "PREPARE TRANSACTION" (free): the participant side of 2PC in a real database: what preparing does, and the warnings about held locks, VACUUM and forgotten prepared transactions. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-prepare-transaction.html
- PostgreSQL documentation, "Two-Phase Transactions" (free): two paragraphs: the three 2PC commands, the XA model, and why the prepared state should be short. https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/two-phase.html
- Cockroach Labs blog, "Parallel Commits: An atomic commit protocol for globally distributed transactions" (free): why classic 2PC is blocking and slow, and how a production database makes it safe by replicating the commit decision through consensus. https://www.cockroachlabs.com/blog/parallel-commits/
- AWS Prescriptive Guidance, "Saga orchestration pattern" (free): the 2PC phases, why database-per-service rules 2PC out, issues to plan for (idempotency, isolation, single point of failure) and a Step Functions example with compensations. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/cloud-design-patterns/saga-orchestration.html
- Azure Architecture Center, "Saga distributed transactions pattern" (free): compensable, pivot and retryable transactions, and the trade-offs of choreography vs. orchestration. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/saga

Lab (1 h):
Split accounts and payments, each with its own database in Compose, talking over HTTP.
In labs, use AI only to clarify concepts, never to write TCM code.

description.en:
Module 5: Messaging and events.
Start with 10 min of flashcard review in Anki (due cards only).

DSA (30 min):
- Course Schedule (cycle detection in a directed graph (3-color DFS)): https://leetcode.com/problems/course-schedule/
Same idea as deadlock detection in a wait-for graph.
Timebox 30 min, no AI. Stuck after 20 min: read only the approach in the editorial, then code it yourself and mark the problem "redo".

Reading (2 h):
- Course text: The log, partitions and producers (written for this course): read this first. It explains the day's concepts and says which sections of the references below to read next. https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/lessons/05-messaging-and-events/day-1.md
- Jay Kreps, "The Log: What every software engineer should know about real-time data's unifying abstraction" (free): queues vs. logs, offsets and consumers. https://engineering.linkedin.com/distributed-systems/log-what-every-software-engineer-should-know-about-real-time-datas-unifying
- Gwen Shapira et al., "Kafka: The Definitive Guide", 2nd edition, chapter 3 (Producers) (free, sign-up required): acks, idempotent producer, partition key and per-key ordering. https://www.confluent.io/resources/kafka-the-definitive-guide-v2/

Lab (1 h):
Redpanda in Compose; create partitioned topics; produce and consume with kcat.
In labs, use AI only to clarify concepts, never to write TCM code.

DSA track: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/DSA.md

description.en:
Module 7: Payments, Pix and reconciliation.
Start with 10 min of flashcard review in Anki (due cards only).

DSA (30 min):
- Rate limiter: token bucket (design + code: allow(userId, now))
No LeetCode link: write a class with allow(userId, now) and unit tests for bursts and refill.
Timebox 30 min, no AI. Stuck after 20 min: read only the approach in the editorial, then code it yourself and mark the problem "redo".

Reading (2 h):
- Course text: The card payment lifecycle and double payments (written for this course): read this first. It explains the day's concepts and says which sections of the references below to read next. https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/lessons/07-payments-pix-reconciliation/day-1.md
- Stripe, "How card payment processing and settlement works" (free): authorization, capture, settlement and the actors (issuer, acquirer, card network, gateway). https://stripe.com/resources/more/credit-card-payment-authorization-and-transaction-settlement-process
- Stripe documentation, "The Payment Intents API" (free): a payment modeled as a state machine. https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents
- Airbnb Engineering, "Avoiding Double Payments in a Distributed Payments System" (free): a real payment system design: idempotency, retries and unknown outcomes. https://medium.com/airbnb-engineering/avoiding-double-payments-in-a-distributed-payments-system-2981f6b070bb

Lab (1 h):
Two fake acquirers that authorize, capture and produce a daily settlement CSV.
In labs, use AI only to clarify concepts, never to write TCM code.

description.en:
Checkpoint 2 (M5 to M7). Today is the one new topic of this week: cross-border payments.

DSA (30 min):
Re-solve 2 problems you marked "redo" in weeks 6 to 8, from scratch, no hints.
No AI.

Reading (2 h):
- Course text: Cross-border payments (written for this course): read this first. It explains the day's concepts and says which sections of the references below to read next. https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/lessons/checkpoint-2-cross-border-payments/day-1.md
- Wise, "What is a correspondent bank?" (free): how correspondent banks, nostro and vostro accounts move SWIFT payments, and why each hop deducts fees. Note the two account definitions. https://wise.com/us/blog/what-is-a-correspondent-bank
- ING Wholesale Banking, "ISO 20022 SWIFT CBPR+ update" (free): the MT to ISO 20022 mapping (MT103 to pacs.008, returns as pacs.004) and the migration dates. Note which message replaces which. https://www.ingwb.com/en/service/payments-and-collections/iso20022-swift-cbpr-update
- Stripe documentation, "Enable currency conversion using the FX Quotes API" (free): a real FX quote: reference rate, fee, lock premium, lock duration, early expiry and the error for an expired quote. Note how to lock the rate the customer saw. https://docs.stripe.com/payments/custom/localize-prices/fx-quotes-api
- Wise Platform documentation, "Transfer statuses" (free): the states of a real cross-border transfer, from waiting for funds to paid out or bounced back. Map them onto your own state machine. https://docs.wise.com/guides/product/send-money/tracking/transfer-statuses
- Banco Central do Brasil, "Cartilha de Câmbio 2026" (free): official BCB guide (in Portuguese): who may operate câmbio, international transfers through eFX providers, and the VET. Note what the VET includes. https://www.bcb.gov.br/content/estabilidadefinanceira/politica_cambial/Cartilha_cambio_2026.pdf

Lab (1 h):
On paper, design a cross-border transfer from a BRL wallet to a USD account: quote, lock, debit, convert, pay out, reconcile. Draw the state machine, the quote row and the ledger entries per currency, and mark where idempotency and reconciliation keys live.

DSA track: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/DSA.md

details.en:
Checkpoint 2 (M5 to M7). Today is the one new topic of this week: cross-border payments.

#### DSA (30 min)
Re-solve 2 problems you marked "redo" in weeks 6 to 8, from scratch, no hints.
No AI.

#### Reading (2 h)
- [Course text: Cross-border payments](https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/lessons/checkpoint-2-cross-border-payments/day-1.md) *(written for this course)*: read this first. It explains the day's concepts and says which sections of the references below to read next.
- [Wise, "What is a correspondent bank?"](https://wise.com/us/blog/what-is-a-correspondent-bank) *(free)*: how correspondent banks, nostro and vostro accounts move SWIFT payments, and why each hop deducts fees. Note the two account definitions.
- [ING Wholesale Banking, "ISO 20022 SWIFT CBPR+ update"](https://www.ingwb.com/en/service/payments-and-collections/iso20022-swift-cbpr-update) *(free)*: the MT to ISO 20022 mapping (MT103 to pacs.008, returns as pacs.004) and the migration dates. Note which message replaces which.
- [Stripe documentation, "Enable currency conversion using the FX Quotes API"](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/custom/localize-prices/fx-quotes-api) *(free)*: a real FX quote: reference rate, fee, lock premium, lock duration, early expiry and the error for an expired quote. Note how to lock the rate the customer saw.
- [Wise Platform documentation, "Transfer statuses"](https://docs.wise.com/guides/product/send-money/tracking/transfer-statuses) *(free)*: the states of a real cross-border transfer, from waiting for funds to paid out or bounced back. Map them onto your own state machine.
- [Banco Central do Brasil, "Cartilha de Câmbio 2026"](https://www.bcb.gov.br/content/estabilidadefinanceira/politica_cambial/Cartilha_cambio_2026.pdf) *(free)*: official BCB guide (in Portuguese): who may operate câmbio, international transfers through eFX providers, and the VET. Note what the VET includes.

#### Lab (1 h)
On paper, design a cross-border transfer from a BRL wallet to a USD account: quote, lock, debit, convert, pay out, reconcile. Draw the state machine, the quote row and the ledger entries per currency, and mark where idempotency and reconciliation keys live.

description.en:
Module 8: Security, compliance and risk.
Start with 10 min of flashcard review in Anki (due cards only).

DSA (30 min):
- LRU Cache (hash map + doubly linked list): https://leetcode.com/problems/lru-cache/
Timebox 30 min, no AI. Stuck after 20 min: read only the approach in the editorial, then code it yourself and mark the problem "redo".

Reading (2 h):
- Course text: Hashing, encryption, keys and mTLS (written for this course): read this first. It explains the day's concepts and says which sections of the references below to read next. https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/lessons/08-security-compliance-risk/day-1.md
- OWASP, "Cryptographic Storage Cheat Sheet" (free): hashing vs. encryption vs. HMAC, and key management basics. https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cryptographic_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html
- Cloudflare Learning, "What is mutual TLS (mTLS)?" (free): TLS and mTLS between services and with partners. https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/access-management/what-is-mutual-tls/
- AWS KMS Developer Guide, "AWS KMS cryptography essentials" (free): KMS vs. HSM, envelope encryption and key rotation. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/kms-cryptography.html

Lab (1 h):
Vault in dev mode (or LocalStack KMS) in Compose; encrypt and decrypt from the CLI.
In labs, use AI only to clarify concepts, never to write TCM code.

Flashcards guide: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/FLASHCARDS.md
DSA track: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/DSA.md
Module page: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/modules/08-security-compliance-risk.md

description.en:
Module 8: Security, compliance and risk.

DSA (30 min):
- LFU Cache (2/2) (hash map + frequency buckets): https://leetcode.com/problems/lfu-cache/
Finish, then test eviction ties (same frequency, least recently used goes first).
Timebox 30 min, no AI. Stuck after 20 min: read only the approach in the editorial, then code it yourself and mark the problem "redo".

Reading (2 h):
- Course text: Tokens, authorization, fraud limits and KYC (written for this course): read this first. It explains the day's concepts and says which sections of the references below to read next. https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/lessons/08-security-compliance-risk/day-3.md
- RFC 9700, "Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security" (free): the attacks it describes and the recommended defenses. https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9700
- OWASP, "JSON Web Token Cheat Sheet" (free): common JWT pitfalls. https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/JSON_Web_Token_Cheat_Sheet.html
- OWASP, "API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization" (free): per-resource authorization. https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa1-broken-object-level-authorization/
- Stripe documentation, "Fraud prevention rules" (free): limits and velocity checks in practice. https://docs.stripe.com/radar/rules
- Banco Central do Brasil, Circular nº 3.978/2020 (Portuguese) (free): KYC and anti-money-laundering duties; skim the structure. https://normativos.bcb.gov.br/Lists/Normativos/Attachments/50905/Circ_3978_v3_P.pdf

Lab (1 h):
Capstone prep: test webhook client and task list. No TCM code.
In labs, use AI only to clarify concepts, never to write TCM code.

description.en:
Module 9: Resilience, high availability and consensus.

DSA (30 min):
- Task Scheduler (greedy + max-heap): https://leetcode.com/problems/task-scheduler/
Timebox 30 min, no AI. Stuck after 20 min: read only the approach in the editorial, then code it yourself and mark the problem "redo".

Reading (2 h):
- Course text: Overload, backlogs and consensus (written for this course): read this first. It explains the day's concepts and says which sections of the references below to read next. https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/lessons/09-resilience-and-consensus/day-2.md
- Amazon Builders' Library, "Avoiding insurmountable queue backlogs" (free): backlogs, prioritization and dropping work. https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/avoiding-insurmountable-queue-backlogs/
- Amazon Builders' Library, "Using load shedding to avoid overload" (free): load shedding and rate limiting. https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/
- Amazon Builders' Library, "Leader election in distributed systems" (free): why systems use a leader, how Amazon elects one with leases, and the stale-leader problem (GC pauses, checking the lease before side effects). https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/leader-election-in-distributed-systems/
- etcd documentation, "FAQ" (free): quorum and failure tolerance per cluster size, why odd member counts, why at most seven members, and how quorum avoids split brain. https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/faq/
- etcd documentation, "Failure modes" (free): what happens on leader failure, majority failure and network partition: election time, queued writes, and why committed writes are never lost. https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/op-guide/failures/
- etcd documentation, "Tuning" (free): heartbeat interval and election timeout: defaults (100 ms, 1000 ms) and how to size them from round-trip time. https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/tuning/
- HashiCorp Consul documentation, "Consensus" (free): a one-page Raft overview from a product that runs it: follower, candidate, leader, when an entry is committed, and the deployment table. https://developer.hashicorp.com/consul/docs/concept/consensus
- Cockroach Labs documentation, "Replication Layer" (free): the Raft section: Raft groups, heartbeats, randomized election timeouts, fault tolerance by replication factor, and snapshots. https://docs.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/architecture/replication-layer
- Patroni documentation, "Introduction" (free): optional: which consensus stores (etcd, Consul, ZooKeeper, Kubernetes) a real Postgres failover tool relies on. https://patroni.readthedocs.io/en/latest/
- The Raft Consensus Algorithm, "Raft" site with visualization (links to The Secret Lives of Data walkthrough) (free): watch an election and log replication in the interactive visualization; then follow the guided walkthrough at thesecretlivesofdata.com/raft. https://raft.github.io/

Explicit timeouts and a circuit breaker (opossum) on the provider; measure again.
In labs, use AI only to clarify concepts, never to write TCM code.

- Amazon Builders' Library, "Using load shedding to avoid overload" (gratuito): load shedding e rate limiting. https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/using-load-shedding-to-avoid-overload/

- Documentação do etcd, "FAQ" (gratuito): quorum e tolerância a falhas por tamanho de cluster, por que números ímpares de membros, por que no máximo sete membros e como o quorum evita split brain. https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/faq/

- Documentação do Patroni, "Introduction" (gratuito): opcional: de quais stores de consenso (etcd, Consul, ZooKeeper, Kubernetes) uma ferramenta real de failover de Postgres depende. https://patroni.readthedocs.io/en/latest/

Laboratório (1 h):
Timeouts explícitos e circuit breaker (opossum) no provedor; medir de novo.

CAPSTONE DAY RULE: everything is done WITHOUT AI. No ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot or AI autocomplete in the editor. Allowed: official docs, books, your own notes and previous labs. Whatever doesn't fit today becomes cut scope for the next checkpoint; the deadline does not move.

description.en:
Module 10: Observability and operations.
CAPSTONE DAY RULE: everything is done WITHOUT AI. No ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot or AI autocomplete in the editor. Allowed: official docs, books, your own notes and previous labs. Whatever doesn't fit today becomes cut scope for the next checkpoint; the deadline does not move.

Today, in order:
4. (45 min) Double-charge detector with an alert.
5. (30 min) Inject a double charge and confirm the alert fires.
6. (1 h) Runbook and postmortem; docs/m10.md.

Delivery (last 30 min):
- Final commit tagged m10.
- Record the mastery test (2 min, no notes): "Without any customer complaining, how would you know that 2% of payments are being charged twice?"
- Listen to the recording and turn every gap into a flashcard (5 to 10 cards, tag gap), then tick the module in your PROGRESS.md.

Flashcards guide: https://github.com/guiferpa/fintech-tech-course/blob/main/FLASHCARDS.md
